D015-D005_h001.question:
It’s been a little over a year now that I’ve just felt…flat, like there’s a weight on me all the time. I used to crochet on my breaks and go out dancing with my sister on weekends. Now I just go home after my shift and sit in front of the TV, not really watching, just staring. Nothing feels worth the effort.

At the booth, I find myself forgetting simple things—who just paid, where I put the change drawer key. I’ll lose track of what lane a car went through, and I feel stupid, like my head is full of fog. I keep thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I don’t have a plan or anything, but the thought of not being here anymore comes up a lot.

Sometimes when I’m working, I get this crawling feeling on my arms or neck, like bugs are on me, but there’s nothing there. And I’ve started feeling like some drivers are talking about me, or that the radio songs are hinting at me specifically, like there’s some message I’m supposed to catch. I’m not sure if I’m imagining it, but it makes me nervous and more withdrawn.
D015-D005_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h001.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h002.question:
I guess this really started getting bad a little over a year ago. I’ve just felt…low all the time. It’s like there’s a gray film over everything. I still do my routes, but I don’t get any enjoyment out of it anymore—no real feeling when I come home, even with my wife and the kids. Things I used to look forward to—listening to games on the radio, stopping at my favorite diners—now it all feels flat.

I can’t seem to make simple choices. I’ll stand in front of the closet in the morning, staring at shirts, or sit with a menu at a truck stop and just freeze. It’s embarrassing. I’m slower getting loads out because I keep second‑guessing every little thing.

A lot of nights I lie in the sleeper cab thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I’m not planning anything, but sometimes I wish the truck would just…not make it.

On top of that, I’m convinced something’s wrong inside my body—like my organs are rotting or poisoned—even though tests keep coming back fine. Sometimes, especially when I’m alone driving at night, I smell this awful, chemical‑rotting odor in the cab that no one else seems to notice. It makes me worry there’s something seriously wrong with me that doctors are missing.
D015-D005_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h002.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h003.question:
It’s hard to put into words. For a little over a year now, it’s felt like something inside me has gone hollow. Not exactly sad all the time, more like…nothing. I go into the workshop, stare at the wood, and just can’t bring myself to care how it turns out. I used to enjoy talking through designs with clients, but lately I avoid calls, ignore texts from friends, even my sister. It all feels like too much effort.

My head feels slow, like it’s full of sawdust. Simple things—measuring, planning a project—take forever because I can’t think straight. Sometimes, when I go to bed, I catch myself wishing I just wouldn’t wake up. I’m not planning to do anything; I’m just tired of existing like this.

I keep having this strong sense that something terrible is coming, like the world is winding down, rotting from the inside. It doesn’t feel like a worry; it feels certain. Every now and then, usually when I’m alone in the shop late, I see people standing in the corners or near the door. When I look directly, they’re gone, but in the moment they seem as real as anyone.
D015-D005_h003.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h003.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h004.question:
I’ve been feeling low for what feels like forever now… maybe a little over a year. It’s like this gray film over everything. Even finishing a chapter for a client, which used to give me a bit of a rush, just feels pointless. I don’t really enjoy anything anymore—books, movies, even seeing my friends’ messages. I mostly ignore them.

Making simple choices has become weirdly hard. I can stare at my closet for 20 minutes trying to pick a shirt or scroll through delivery apps and then just give up and not eat. It’s like my brain freezes whenever I have to decide something.

Sometimes, especially when I’m walking near the subway tracks or crossing a busy street, I get these sudden urges to just… step off, or walk into the traffic. It’s not like I’ve planned anything, but the impulse is there and it scares me.

There are also these… experiences I’m not sure how to explain. I keep feeling like this editor I worked with once is secretly in love with me—like the way he phrases his emails is coded somehow. And every now and then I hear someone say my name, or a voice commenting on what I’m doing, but when I look around there’s no one there. I can’t tell if it’s just stress or something worse, but it’s making it harder to work and to trust my own head.
D015-D005_h004.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h004.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h005.question:
I don’t really feel much of anything anymore. It’s been like this for a little over a year. Even when something “good” happens at work or with my kids, it’s like I’m watching someone else’s life. I go through the motions, but I don’t feel joy or closeness, even with my husband. Things I used to enjoy—reading, dinners with friends—just feel flat, so I mostly avoid them.

I’ve also been having a lot of trouble with my memory and concentration. I’ll walk into a room and forget why, misplace my phone or keys constantly, lose track in the middle of interviews or meetings. For someone in HR, that’s… not great. I’ve made small mistakes in emails and scheduling that I never used to make.

Sometimes I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or I imagine stepping in front of a train on my commute. I don’t have a plan, but those thoughts come more often than I’d like to admit.

On top of that, I’ve started feeling like people at work are watching me, like there’s some sort of monitoring going on behind the scenes. Occasionally I see shadowy figures or shapes out of the corner of my eye—like someone standing in the hallway—but when I look directly, there’s no one there. I can’t tell if I’m just exhausted and stressed or if something is really wrong with me.
D015-D005_h005.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h005.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h006.question:
I guess this really started about four months ago. It’s like something inside me just…shut off. I go to the office, I sit in front of the files, but there’s nothing there emotionally—no anger, no interest, not even real anxiety, just this hollow, numb feeling. I used to get worked up over cases; now I’m barely keeping up, missing deadlines, avoiding clients.

At night my mind goes over every mistake I’ve ever made—botched cross‑examinations from ten years ago, small things I said to my ex‑wife, not being around enough for my son. I replay them until 3 or 4 a.m., telling myself I ruined everything. It feels like I don’t deserve the life I have.

Lately I’ve been convinced something terrible is coming. Not just for me—like the whole world is on the verge of collapsing. It’s not exactly a thought, more like a certainty that everything is about to end. Sometimes, when I’m sitting alone, I feel things crawling on my skin or a hand brushing my arm, and there’s no one there.

About a month ago I gathered up some leftover pain meds and alcohol and planned to take them all. I even wrote out instructions for my will. I stopped at the last minute, but it scared me enough to finally come in.
D015-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D015-D005_h006.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h007.question:
I guess this started around four months ago. At first I thought it was just burnout from residency, but it’s like something switched off inside me. I don’t really feel much of anything now—no real sadness, but also no joy. Even when I match a tough diagnosis or a patient thanks me, it’s like watching someone else’s life. I’m just going through the motions on the wards.

At the same time, I’ve become convinced I’ve caused harm in ways that don’t quite make sense. When something bad happens in the hospital—a code, a complication—I feel sure it’s because of me, even when I wasn’t on that service. I keep thinking if I’d studied more, prayed more, done something different, those people wouldn’t have suffered.

That feeds into these thoughts about ending things. I’ve worked out, in more detail than I’m comfortable admitting, where I’d do it and how to avoid being found too quickly.

What’s confusing is there are moments where I feel the opposite—that I’m meant for something huge in medicine, like I have some special insight others don’t. And occasionally, especially when I’m exhausted on nights, I see people in the hallway who aren’t there when I look again—faces or figures just at the edge of my vision. It’s been hard to tell what’s just stress and what isn’t, but it’s definitely affecting my work and I’m worried I’m not safe for patients or myself.
D015-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D015-D005_h007.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h008.question:
I’ve been feeling like I’ve hit bottom for about four months now. It’s pretty much every day. I wake up already heavy, like there’s no point. I used to be good at my job—following people, putting pieces together—but lately I just sit in my car outside a case address and stare. I keep thinking I’m useless, that no one would really miss me. I don’t have a plan or anything, but the idea of just not being here anymore comes up a lot, especially at night.

At the same time, there’s this other side of it that doesn’t totally fit with feeling so low. Sometimes I’m convinced I’m meant for something huge, like I’m the only one who can really see the truth about people, almost like I’ve got some special ability. It sounds strange even saying it here. And there are these voices—usually when I’m alone on a stakeout or trying to fall asleep. They’re not my thoughts. Sometimes they criticize me, sometimes they tell me I’m important, but either way, no one else is there when I hear them.
D015-D005_h008.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D015-D005_h008.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h009.question:
It’s been about four months now where I just feel like I’m falling apart. I cry at the drop of a hat—at work, in the car between showings, even during open houses if something small goes wrong. I keep replaying tiny mistakes, like misplacing paperwork or snapping at a client, and I feel like I’m this terrible person who ruins everything. I keep thinking my husband and kids would be better off without me. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but a lot of nights I lie there wishing I just wouldn’t wake up.

Sometimes I smell this strong scent—like cigarette smoke or cheap perfume—when there’s nothing there. It’ll happen in my car or in the kitchen, and no one else seems to notice it. All of this is making it really hard to focus on my clients or even just get through the day.
D015-D005_h009.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D015-D005_h009.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h010.question:
I’d say this started about four months ago. At first I just felt… switched off. It’s like someone turned the saturation down on everything. I go to the lab, I run code, I answer emails, but it all feels mechanical, like I’m watching myself do it. I used to get excited about a good dataset or a new paper; now I mostly feel nothing, or this dull heaviness.

At the same time I’ve become obsessed with the idea that things going wrong at work or at home are my fault. If a pipeline crashes, I replay every step and convince myself I’ve sabotaged the project. If my husband seems quiet, I’m sure I’ve ruined his life by being like this. I keep thinking I deserve something bad to happen, and there are days when this loops into “maybe everyone would be better if I just weren’t here.” I don’t have a plan, but those thoughts about not wanting to exist show up a lot.

Lately I’ve also been convinced there’s something wrong inside my body—like my organs are rotting, even though tests are normal. And a few times, especially when I’m tired, I’ve seen people standing in the hallway or in the lab who disappear when I look twice. I’m not sure how all of this fits together; it just makes it harder to function and to trust my own mind.
D015-D005_h010.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D015-D005_h010.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h011.question:
I’ve been feeling off for around seven months now. I still go to the gym to coach my clients, but it’s getting harder to function. I cry a lot, usually when I’m alone in the locker room or at home. It’ll hit me out of nowhere, and I can’t really explain why. I’m sleeping enough hours, but I wake up feeling like I haven’t rested at all, like my body’s heavy and my brain’s already tired before the day even starts.

What really scares me is how quickly my mind just… runs out of energy. Simple things—planning a workout program, answering messages—feel like mental marathons. I lose focus halfway through and just stare at the screen.

Lately I’ve also been feeling like people are watching me or talking about me. Sometimes when I’m walking around the gym, I’m convinced there are cameras hidden, or that some of the regulars are reporting on me to someone. I know it sounds strange, and part of me questions it, but the feeling is really strong, like I’m being monitored or set up somehow. I can’t tell when this all really started, it just kind of blended into everything else.
D015-D005_h011.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h012.question:

D015-D005_h013.question:

D015-D005_h014.question:

D015-D005_h017.question:

D015-D005_h021.question:
I guess the best way to put it is that, for about eight months now, I’ve felt…flat. Not sad in the usual sense, more like someone turned the volume down on everything. My kids, my work, even closing a big deal—none of it stirs much in me. I’m going through the motions with clients, but it feels mechanical, and I’ve been dropping balls at work, missing details I never used to miss.
